newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Jan-Oct investment up 77.7 percent.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Jan-Oct investment up 77.7 percent.

text.p: Slovenia's government sponsored Institute of Macroeconomic Analysis and Development said on Friday registered investments rose 77.7 percent in the first 10 months of 1996 to 236.2 billion tolars ($1.7 billion).
"The highest increase was recorded in the construction of roads, telecommunication and post network sectors. Investment also surged in forestry and industry," the institute said in its latest report.
But it said the extraordinary increase was also partly a result of improvements in the system of registering investments.

The report said 15.5 percent of all investments were financed by bank loans, slightly up on last year. The average lending rate for long-term loans was 12.8 percent, down 2.9 percentage points from last year.
